long_biography.plain_text:
Ralph de la Torre’s surgical work included developing a less invasive technique for open-heart operations. At Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, he led cardiac surgery and established a cardiovascular institute that brought medical and surgical specialties together. The institute coordinated services around patients who needed different forms of cardiovascular care.

His technical work extended into medical information systems. With Justine Carr, he was named as an inventor on a patent for processing clinical information and combining related alerts. The design gathered several clinical triggers into one notification, which could then be sent to a clinician’s device.

confidence.reason: University contemporary surgical account, primary professional interview and official patent claim support distinct clinical organisation and invention. A patent design is not claimed to be a deployed product.
